title: There's no F in Korean… so Zara becomes a turtle 🐢 #learnkorean
caption:
Korean has no F, V or Z sounds, so names change:

Fiona → 피오나 (pi-o-na)
Victor → 빅터 (bik-teo)
Zara → 자라 (ja-ra) — and 자라 is also a soft-shell turtle 🐢
Bob → 밥 (bap) — and 밥 means rice 🍚

Most of the time: F → ㅍ · V → ㅂ · Z → ㅈ

Comment just your first name and I'll write it in Korean ✍️ (first 3 days). Or try it yourself: synk.im/name

alt: A coral felt mascot sits behind a mint felt table with wooden letter blocks spelling FIONA. The F tips off the edge, hits a toy seesaw and launches a Korean block ㅍ into its place; the blocks merge into 피 오 나 (pi-o-na). VICTOR: the ㅂ block bonks the mascot on the head and it goes dizzy, then the blocks become 빅 터 (bik-teo). ZARA becomes 자 라 (ja-ra) — and a felt turtle walks in and carries the blocks on its shell: 자라 = a turtle. Then Bob → 밥 = rice, with the turtle eating a felt bowl of rice. The turtle looks at the viewer: 너는? = And you? Comment your name.
